_comment: MS Harness configuration template. Copy this file, rename it, and fill in the fields for your tool. Remove all '_comment' keys before use.

project.name: My Analysis Project
project.description: Optional: one sentence describing what this campaign is studying.

tool._comment: 'adapter' must match the name of a subdirectory under tools/. Create that directory with input_processor.py, output_processor.py, and run_model.sh.
tool.name: My Tool Name
tool.domain: Brief domain label, e.g. 'cybersecurity', 'traffic simulation', 'supply chain'
tool.description: Plain language: what does this tool simulate? One to three sentences.

adapter_config._comment: Any key-value pairs here are passed as-is to input_processor.py and run_model.sh. Put tool executable paths, data file paths, and run-time settings here.

inputs._comment: Set discovery to 'dynamic' if your input_processor.discover_inputs() reads parameters from a file at runtime. Set to 'static' and define a 'parameters' list if the schema is fixed.
inputs.description: Brief description of what the input parameters represent.
inputs.sme_notes: What do you already know about which inputs tend to drive bad outcomes? This text is fed to the AI for interpretation.

outputs._comment: 'id' must exactly match the key returned by output_processor.process(). Add one entry per metric your tool produces.
outputs.description: What does this metric mean? What are its units and range?

objective._comment: critical_metric must match one of the output ids above.
objective._comment_direction: 'below' = low values are bad (e.g. resilience). 'above' = high values are bad (e.g. cost, casualties).
objective._comment_quantile: 0.5 = bottom half of outcomes is 'critical'. Lower values narrow the critical set; higher values broaden it.
objective._comment_threshold: Optional. Fixed critical threshold in the metric's own units (e.g. 20 = resilience <= 20% is critical). If omitted, the threshold is the critical_threshold_quantile of the FIRST LHS sweep and stays fixed for later targeted sweeps.
objective.surprise_definition: What would it mean for a critical scenario to be surprising? Describe the combination of inputs that would be unexpected given domain knowledge.
objective._comment_potential: How should node importance be measured? Options: 'paths_to_exit' (topological — fraction of source-to-exit paths through each node), 'betweenness' (graph centrality), 'likelihood' (mean LHS weight — use when there is no graph structure), 'sme' (the nodes listed in sme_expected_drivers — critical scenarios WITHOUT those drivers elevated score as surprising, i.e. surprise = contradicting the SME).
objective._comment_drivers: Optional. Input ids the SME expects to drive critical outcomes, as a list or {id: importance}. Required for element_potential 'sme'; otherwise shown to the AI and used to flag, per top scenario, which expected drivers were elevated.
objective.sme_context: Summarize what you already know about this system: which inputs are high-impact, what failure modes are already understood, and what surprises you are trying to find. This is placed in the AI's system preamble for every interpretation, proposal and chat — framed as the SME's prior expectations to be tested, not as fact.

sampling._comment: initial_n: scenarios in the first LHS sweep. sweep_budget: total scenario budget across all sweeps. Targeted follow-ups consume followup_fraction * sweep_budget each.
